title: Choose the landing page's structure
question: The world is settled (the Site Drawing Set). Pick how the page walks a judge from one line to the live demo.

options.label: The stamp chain
options.lineage: a document passed desk to desk, stamped at each check
options.thesis: One claim, "Windows complete: 12", walks down the page collecting a stamp at every check until it lands on its outcome.
options.viewport: The highlighted letter line at left; a vertical chain of five numbered stations descends right, station 1 already stamped; Open the Flat 302 demo sits in the sheet's title block.
options.risk: Five stations is a lot of scroll for a judge with two minutes, so each station has to land in one glance.

raised.raise: Rank by type size alone: the outcome stamp is the largest mark on the page, each earlier check one size smaller.
Every station is a numbered, linkable sheet detail (A1 to A5), so the demo video can cut straight to one.
One ground owns each station whole: blueprint for the plan stations, paper for the document ones, never a card on a neutral page.
Only the station in view carries safety orange; the rest of the chain waits in ink.
The demo opens on the same room the visitor was reading about, so reading and trying are one step apart.

options.label: The tally story
options.lineage: a site progress board, filled in room by room
options.thesis: A twelve-segment tally stays on screen while the page walks Flat 302 room by room, filling as each room is judged and ending at 10 of 12.
options.viewport: 9 of 12 windows verified at display scale over the twelve segments; the plan beneath with the next room outlined; the demo button beside the count.
options.risk: It leans on the number, so judges still have to learn why Not seen yet isn't a failure.

options.label: Paper vs evidence
options.lineage: a drawing sheet folded down its centre
options.thesis: The sheet splits on its fold: what a buyer pays against today on the left, what SiteProof shows on the right, line for line.
options.viewport: Left half the demand letter as a bare paper claim; right half the same lines with frames, outlines and stamps; the demo button sits on the fold.
options.risk: A side-by-side can read as catching the builder out, so the copy has to keep the 'gets builders paid' flip.

options.label: The evidence line
options.lineage: a museum provenance ribbon, fused into the drawing set
options.thesis: One safety-orange evidence line runs from the quoted claim through clip, room tag, count and frame to the report; where evidence is missing it turns to dashed thread.
options.viewport: The line enters from the quoted claim at top left and threads down through the plan of Flat 302; the kitchen gap is dashed thread beside its 5-second request.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the evidence chain is the product and a gap drawn as thread makes Not seen yet honest. Judges don't know museum provenance, so it wins on clarity, not identification.
options.risk: The line has to stay legible on a phone; a decorative line is slop.

options.label: Fight poster
options.thesis: Builder versus buyer across a gold VS.
options.viewport: Two names colliding at a versus mark.
options.case: Declined on product truth: a versus frame is the policing story SiteProof exists to refuse.
options.risk: Turns proof of progress into a fight.

options.label: Teletext service
options.thesis: SiteProof as numbered pages on black.
options.viewport: Page 302 with the report built from blocks.
options.case: Declined: replaces the drawing-set world with a retro novelty judges would read as a gimmick.

options.label: Seedbed lobes
options.thesis: Floating white capsules on a green field.
options.viewport: Green field, pill nav, grotesque headline.
options.case: Declined: it's the generic product page the brief asked to avoid, and rounded pills break the square drawing set.
options.kept: One ground owns each region whole.

options.label: Luminescent understory
options.thesis: Evidence glowing like spores in the dark.
options.viewport: A dark field where rooms pulse as you approach.
options.case: Declined: mood over proof, and glow reads as decoration in sunlight.
options.kept: Only the focus carries the brightest mark.

options.label: HyperCard stack
options.thesis: The pitch as a stack of linked black-and-white cards.
options.viewport: One card with painted links to the next.
options.case: Declined: one-bit loses the three outcome colours, which carry meaning here.
options.risk: Loses Verified / Short / Not seen yet at a glance.
options.kept: Reading and trying one step apart.
